topics.title: Electric Charge
topics.description: The fundamental property of matter that causes electromagnetic phenomena.
objectives: Explain the nature of electric charge and its conservation
Apply Coulomb's law to compute forces between charges
Distinguish conductors from insulators
Describe charging by conduction and induction

topics.title: Electric Field
topics.description: The vector field representing the force per unit charge at every point in space.
objectives: Define electric field as force per unit charge
Draw and interpret field lines
Compute fields from point charges and distributions
Understand superposition of electric fields

topics.title: Gauss's Law
topics.description: Relates total electric flux through a closed surface to the enclosed charge.
objectives: Define electric flux
State Gauss's law in integral form
Apply Gauss's law to symmetric charge distributions
Derive field inside/outside a uniformly charged sphere

topics.title: Electric Potential
topics.description: Potential energy per unit charge — the scalar counterpart to the electric field.
objectives: Define electric potential and potential difference (voltage)
Relate potential to electric field via the gradient
Calculate potential from point charges
Understand equipotential surfaces

topics.title: DC Circuits
topics.description: Analysis of direct-current circuits using Ohm's law and Kirchhoff's rules.
objectives: Apply Ohm's law V=IR
Analyze series and parallel resistor networks
Apply Kirchhoff's current and voltage laws
Compute power dissipation in resistors

topics.title: Magnetism
topics.description: Magnetic forces, fields, and the behavior of moving charges in magnetic fields.
objectives: Describe magnetic force on moving charges (Lorentz force)
Compute magnetic field from current-carrying wires
Apply the right-hand rule
Understand magnetic dipoles and bar magnets

topics.title: Faraday's Law and Induction
topics.description: A changing magnetic flux induces an EMF — the foundation of generators and transformers.
objectives: State Faraday's law of induction
Apply Lenz's law to determine direction of induced current
Compute induced EMF for moving conductors
Understand mutual and self-inductance
